edges.description: Reported in a single p.F507S case and attributed to type I interferon-mediated suppression of lipoprotein lipase; a contribution of treatment could not be excluded, and the triglycerides normalized on JAK inhibition.
Neonatal-onset cases show an Aicardi-Goutieres-like interferonopathy picture with cerebral calcification, consistent with the type I interferon excess.
Neurological complications are frequent; developmental delay accompanies the interferon-driven CNS involvement.
White-matter lesions (leukoencephalopathy) are part of the interferonopathy-like CNS picture.

nodes.description: Germline missense variants in TLR7 (p.Y264H, and others such as p.F507S) confer a gain of function. TLR7 is an endosomal sensor of viral single-stranded RNA that binds guanosine; the variants selectively increase its sensing of guanosine and the self-ligand 2',3'-cGMP.

nodes.description: An oral dual TLR7-TLR8 antagonist directly targets the lesion; in phase II trials it durably suppressed the interferon signature in all patients. Important caveats: the trials were in general (polygenic) SLE, not in TLR7 gain-of-function disease, and the primary dose-response endpoint was met only in cutaneous lupus erythematosus, so the clinical benefit is not established for TLR7 GOF specifically.
